decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet cardboard display sits squarely in the firm's core display business, so it uses existing capacity at little cost and gives no performance shortfall that would trigger search for other uses.
Pegboard-back shelf displays are a standard retail format close to the established offer, so they likely meet aspirations in a stable market and are cheap to carry with the firm's slack.
The basic quarter-pallet display is a staple of point-of-sale display demand and fits existing production fully, so there is no reason to drop it.
The eighth-pallet display complements the quarter-pallet range for smaller placements and adds little cost, so keeping it fits a firm whose results are holding steady.
The wooden pallet departs from the firm's cardboard competence and is more exposed to falling short, but the large firm's slack lets it carry the product while results remain uncertain.
Demand for displays of physical media is declining, which raises the chance of a shortfall against aspiration, yet the format can be reused for other goods at low cost, so it is kept for now.
